title: Execution Trace Cache Replacing Traditional L1 Instruction Cache
decision: Implement an Execution Trace Cache (TC) that stores decoded micro-ops (uops) in execution flow order rather than storing raw x86 instruction bytes.
alternatives_or_rejected: A conventional L1 instruction cache holding raw x86 bytes, which requires instruction decoding on the critical fetch path during every cycle.
rationale: x86 instruction decoding is complex and variable-length. Removing the decoder from the main execution loop eliminates instruction decode bandwidth bottlenecks and reduces pipeline depth for branch target fetches, allowing higher clock frequency scaling.
outcome: Delivered up to 3 uops per cycle directly to the execution pipeline, bypassing instruction decode logic on trace cache hits.

title: Double-Pumped 2x Clock Rapid Execution Engine
decision: Operate the core simple integer ALUs at twice the main core clock frequency.
alternatives_or_rejected: Operating the ALUs at 1x core clock frequency and using wider parallel issue logic.
rationale: Running simple ALUs at 2x clock speed provides an effective 0.5 main-clock-cycle latency for basic arithmetic and logic operations, allowing dependent integer instruction chains to execute with minimal latency while keeping execution unit area small.
outcome: Achieved sub-cycle latency (0.5 clock cycles) for basic integer operations, significantly speeding up dependent scalar integer code loops.

title: 20-Stage Hyper-Pipelined Core Design
decision: Implement a 20-stage deep pipeline (Hyper-Pipelined Technology) for instruction execution.
alternatives_or_rejected: Maintaining a shallower ~10-stage pipeline similar to the Pentium III (P6 microarchitecture).
rationale: Reducing the logic depth and gate delays per pipeline stage allows the processor to scale to substantially higher clock frequencies on the same manufacturing process node.
outcome: Enabled frequency targets above 1.4 GHz at product launch, accepting a higher branch misprediction latency penalty that had to be offset by improved branch prediction.

title: Low-Latency 8KB L1 Data Cache with 2-Cycle Access
decision: Use a small 8KB L1 data cache optimized for a 2-clock-cycle load-to-use access latency.
alternatives_or_rejected: A larger 16KB or 32KB L1 data cache with 3 to 4 clock cycles of access latency.
rationale: At multi-gigahertz clock frequencies, minimizing load-to-use latency for dependent instructions is more critical for performance than increasing L1 capacity, provided the L2 cache has sufficient bandwidth.
outcome: Delivered 2-cycle load access latency to the execution engine, backed by a high-bandwidth 256-bit wide interface to the L2 cache.
